title: Packet Alley
tagline: Keep a city connected. See what each packet does.
panel_edits_hint: Click a ✎ on the map to change the network right there — or use the choices here.
point_hint: Click a glowing machine on the map to send it there.
predict_hint: Inspect the glowing devices if you like, then say what will happen.
evidence_hint: Inspect the glowing devices first, then make your prediction.
commit_hint: Pick your prediction above to commit and run.
predict_wrong: Your prediction did not match the run. Inspect the trace and try a practice case.
log_empty: Run the level to see what each packet does, step by step.
log_none_match: No log lines match these filters.
about_host: A computer on the network. It sends and receives packets, and it has one IP address.
about_printer: A printer. On the network it behaves like any other computer with one address.
about_server: A server. It waits for connections and answers requests, such as a web page.
about_hub: A hub is thus a physical layer relay that receives an electrical signal on one of its interfaces, regenerates the signal and transmits it over all its other interfaces. (Computer Networking, Bonaventure — CC BY-SA 3.0)
about_switch: An Ethernet switch understands the format of the Ethernet frames and can selectively forward frames over each interface. For this, each Ethernet switch maintains a MAC address table. The pseudo-code below details how an Ethernet switch forwards Ethernet frames. It first updates its MAC address table with the source address of the frame. (Computer Networking, Bonaventure — CC BY-SA 3.0)
about_router: With the datagram organization, routers use hop-by-hop forwarding. This means that when a router receives a packet that is not destined to itself, it looks up the destination address of the packet in its forwarding table. (Computer Networking, Bonaventure — CC BY-SA 3.0)
f_lost: This one was lost on the cable.
sum_retransmits: {a} frames had to be sent again.
quiz_wrong: Not quite. Pass the level again to retry.
ev_queue_full: {a}'s outgoing line is full; a frame was dropped.
ev_no_gateway: {a} has no gateway, so it cannot reach {b} (off its block {c}).
ev_arp_fail: {a} could not find anyone at {b} on its block.
ev_arp_fail_gw: {a} could not find its gateway {b} on block {c}.
ev_gave_up: {a} gave up after too many tries.
ev_retry: {a} heard nothing back; it is trying again.
ev_timeout: The sender timed out and is resending from segment {b}.
ev_collision: {a}: {b} frames arrived at once and collided.
ev_collision_gave_up: A frame from {a} collided too many times and was dropped.
ev_ttl: {a} dropped a packet from {b} to {c}: it ran out of hops.
ev_arp_fail_router: {a} could not find the next hop {b} on its block.
ev_ignore: {a} ignored a frame addressed to {b} (not its MAC).
ev_ping: {a} was pinged by {b} and is replying.
ev_out_of_order: {a} got segment {b} but wanted {c}; it asks again for the one it wants.
ev_synack: {a} answered a SYN with a SYN-ACK to {b}.
ev_bad_ack: {a} expected to be acknowledged {b} but got {c}; it reset the connection.
ev_was_reset: {a}'s connection was reset by the server.
ev_lost: A frame from {a} to {b} was lost on the cable.
ev_no_entry: {a} has no table entry for {b}, so the frame was dropped.
why_no_gateway: A computer needs a gateway to reach another block.
why_arp_fail: That address is not on this block. Check the address, or send through the router.
why_arp_fail_gw: The gateway address must be a real device on this block.
why_ttl: Each router subtracts one hop. A packet runs out when the trip needs more hops than it was given — or when it loops. Give it more hops, or break the loop.
why_no_route: The router needs a route that covers the destination.
why_collision: A hub lets only one device talk at a time. A switch gives each device its own line.
why_not_mine: The destination address does not match this device.
why_reset: The server answers a proper handshake. Check the steps and the acknowledgement numbers.
why_bad_ack: The third step must acknowledge the server's number plus one.
why_nothing_lost: Nothing was dropped — the goal just was not met in time. Try a change.
why_no_entry: A build switch forwards only by the table you fill. Add a row for that machine, pointing out the right cable.
how_1: Devices sit on the map. Lines between them are cables. Click a device to see what it knows.
how_2: When you run a level, packets ride along the cables. Each packet has its own shape, pattern and letter for what it is; the list beside the map names them. Nothing is told apart by colour alone.
how_3: A ✓ is a delivery, an ✕ is a loss, a ✻ is a collision. The log on the right lists every step in words.
how_4: Click a moving packet to open it up, header by header, from the frame to the IP packet to the TCP segment inside.
how_5: Make the changes the level offers, run it, and watch. Pass the goal to unlock the next level and answer one question for a third star.
err_locked: That level is locked. Pass the one before it, or turn on Teacher mode.
err_quiz_first: Pass the level before answering the question.
err_inspect_first: Inspect the evidence on the map before you commit.
err_predict_first: Mark your prediction before you commit and run.
super_locked: Clear this zone's levels to unlock the build challenge.
build_tier1: ★ it works — now make it cheaper
build_hint_place: Click an open spot on the floor to set down the {a}.
build_hint_wire: Click one machine, then the machine to join it to.
build_hint_wire_from: Now click the machine to connect {a} to.
build_pick_addr: Its address on the shop's block
build_table_hint: For each machine, choose the cable this switch should send its frames out of.
build_route_hint: For each block it can't reach directly, choose the road (the neighbouring router) toward it.
build_step_place: Place a switch, then run a cable from it to each register and to the server.
build_step_addr: Give every register an address on the shop's block (10.0.0.0/24).
build_step_table: Fill the switch's table so it knows which cable leads to each machine.
build_step_cost: Watch the bill — a shorter run of cable costs less. Open when every register is connected.
result_gold: Hidden gold star — one of the cheapest shops anyone has wired!
err_build_max: You have placed all of those you can.
err_build_obstacle: You cannot put a machine on a wall or a counter.
err_build_too_long: That cable would be longer than the reel allows.
err_build_wired: Those two are already joined by a cable.
err_build_crosses: A cable cannot run through the kitchen — route it around.
err_build_water: A cable can't cross the water — run it over a bridge.
err_build_water_place: You can't place a machine on the water — put it on the land.
err_build_two_hosts: A router reaches one machine per block. Put both machines on a switch, then wire the switch to the router.
